findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top-ranked gene with clinical-stage antagonists (reparixin, navarixin, ladarixin, SX-682), yet it has no verbatim-validated literature relations in the graph. Corpus support is indirect: a title-level hit calls CXCR1 and CXCR2 potential neutrophil extracellular trap-related treatment targets in UC (Mendelian randomization, colocalization, transcriptomics), and a CXCL5/CXCR2 axis study links it to neutrophil chemotaxis and immune activation in UC. This is bioinformatic/genetic support, not a UC trial.

The literature states that the axis of CXCL8 with its receptors CXCR1 and CXCR2 participates in UC pathogenesis through PI3K/Akt, MAPK and NF-kappaB signaling. In a blood RNA-seq validation CXCL8 had good diagnostic performance for IBD, but this is IBD-level, not UC-specific, and the evidence is bioinformatic.

A single mechanistic study reports IDO1 elevated in UC patients and colitis mice, driving M1 macrophage polarization via the ER stress GRP78-XBP1 pathway. An IDO inhibitor (methyl-tryptophan) ameliorated DSS colitis (weight loss, colon shortening, severity). Support is preclinical and from one study; IDO1 inhibitors (epacadostat, linrodostat) are oncology-stage, not UC.

CHI3L1 is upregulated in UC patients and correlates with NLRP3 inflammasome expression. It promotes macrophage pyroptosis via a BCAT1/NF-kappaB axis, and NF-kappaB activation reversed the protective effect of CHI3L1 inhibition. A virtual-screen hit (velpatasvir) bound recombinant CHI3L1 at micromolar affinity. No approved CHI3L1 drug; evidence is single-study and preclinical.

MMP1 showed strong diagnostic potential (AUC reported in an UC-associated CRC bioinformatic study), and its transcript correlates with UC disease activity indices (Mayo, Geboes, Robarts) and is modified by mirikizumab. This is a bioinformatic signature plus a trial-biopsy transcriptomic correlation; MMP inhibitors are not validated in UC.

DUOX2 protein is among the most elevated in inflamed UC biopsies versus healthy controls, and is named as a credible biomarker for UC diagnosis and therapy in a bioinformatic study. One herbal formula (TLXDS) reduced UC via inhibiting DUOX2 overexpression, with DUOX2 proposed as its target. Support is consistent but mostly signature and single-study preclinical.

S100A9 expression showed excellent performance in diagnosing active UC in one study. Conversely, in a treatment-response single-cell study S100A9 was downregulated in resident macrophages with response, linking it to a myeloid compartment rather than epithelium. Evidence is bioinformatic and single-cohort.

AQP9 is predominantly expressed in neutrophils (single-cell analysis) and promotes NET formation through JAK2-STAT3-mediated pyroptosis, aggravating epithelial injury in UC mice. The signal is therefore from infiltrating neutrophils, not the epithelium. No drug in the graph; single-study evidence.

SLC26A2 is down-regulated in active UC mucosa versus healthy controls and its decreased level correlates with Mayo score and PUCAI; it is positively associated with CLDN3 and negatively with IL-17A. It is a loss-of-function barrier marker, not a druggable target; one study.

LCN2 is upregulated in UC and, in one study, its expression fell from short-duration UC to long-duration UC to UC-associated cancer while all remained above normal, so it was proposed as a diagnostic marker for UC-associated carcinogenesis. Single-study evidence.

TREM1 has no verbatim relation in the graph, but corpus sentences report that TREM1 activation exacerbates colitis in mice and an elevated TREM1 pathway signature in biopsies is associated with inflamed tissue and treatment resistance in UC. Nangibotide (phase 2) exists in other indications. Preclinical plus biopsy signature.

CD274 (PD-L1) is listed among hub genes for UC positively associated with macrophage infiltration (bioinformatics) and was validated by immunohistochemistry in one hospital series. No verbatim-validated relation in the graph; the PD-L1 drugs are oncology agents and checkpoint blockade direction in UC is not addressed by these sentences.

caveats: Most relations are single-study bioinformatic or murine findings; no approved UC drug is supported directly by these genes in the corpus.
CXCR2, CXCR1, CD274, FCGR2A, JAK2, IL2RA, INHBA, TREM1, CXCL5, PI3, S100A12 and REG1A have strong expression or Open Targets support but no verbatim-validated literature relations in the graph.
The CXCL8 diagnostic result is for IBD from blood, not UC mucosa.
Numbers such as AUC values were not bound to records and are described in words only.
Roughly 40 calls were budgeted; not all top-40 genes were searched individually.
